story: Forsyth Park began in the 1840s on 10 acres given by William Brown Hodgson. It was expanded and named for Georgia Governor John Forsyth in 1851. It covers 30 acres.
The fountain was installed in 1858 and cast by Janes, Beebe & Company. Its design comes from the work of French sculptor Michel Lienard and resembles fountains at the Place de la Concorde in Paris.

The Confederate Memorial was unveiled in 1874 and a bronze soldier was added in 1879. The Fragrant Garden was designed for the blind, and the fountain is ceremonially turned green for St. Patrick's Day.
stops.fact: The fountain is turned green for St. Patrick's Day.
stops.disputed: Many sources say Forsyth donated the land. Wikipedia says William Brown Hodgson gave the first 10 acres.

claims.t: The Forsyth Park fountain was installed in 1858.
Governor Forsyth donated the first 10 acres.
claims.why: William Brown Hodgson donated the first 10 acres.

story: River Street is about 2 miles long along the Savannah River, according to Wikipedia. The south side has rows of former cotton warehouses, some dating from the 1850s.

Factors Walk is built on the middle level of the sloping bluff, with warehouses beneath and Bay Street above. Cotton brokers, called factors, bargained there. The name Factors Row preserves the industry's name.
The pavement is Belgian block with streetcar tracks set in. Large tankers and container ships heading to and from the Port of Savannah sometimes pass within yards of the promenade.
stops.fact: The warehouses were built for the cotton trade.
stops.disputed: A popular claim says the cobblestones are old ship ballast stones. Wikipedia describes Belgian block paving instead.

claims.t: River Street has former cotton warehouses.
claims.why: Wikipedia: terraces of former King Cotton warehouses.

claims.t: The paving is all old ship ballast.
claims.why: A popular story, but Wikipedia describes Belgian block paving.

story: The parish started in 1799. The present cathedral was dedicated on April 30, 1876, and Ephraim Francis Baldwin was its architect, in Gothic Revival style.
A fire destroyed the interior on February 6, 1898. The first Mass in the rebuilt building was held in December 1899, and it was rededicated on October 28, 1900.
It is 214 feet tall overall and has 81 stained-glass windows. Windows installed in 1904 came from Austria-Hungary. Pope Francis made it a minor basilica in January 2020.
stops.fact: It became a minor basilica in 2020.
stops.disputed: Older guides say the basilica title dates to the 1990s. Wikipedia says January 2020.

claims.t: The cathedral was named a basilica in 1996.
claims.why: Pope Francis elevated it in January 2020.

story: Colonial Park Cemetery was established in 1750, when Savannah was the capital of the British Province of Georgia. It closed to burials in 1853 and has been a public park since 1896.
Button Gwinnett, signer of the Declaration of Independence, is buried there, along with Lachlan McIntosh and James Habersham. An estimated 9,000 graves are there.
After Union troops occupied Savannah on December 24, 1864, the cemetery sheltered several hundred Union soldiers. Soldiers allegedly damaged some markers, altering dates and ages.
stops.disputed: The story of soldiers altering headstones is told as a rumor. Wikipedia uses the word allegedly.

claims.t: Union soldiers certainly carved fake dates on gravestones.
claims.why: The story is repeated, but Wikipedia says only that they allegedly altered some markers.
